title: Staging validation and publish playbook for Redwood-verified model performance profiles
creator: Amina Ruiz
description:
Problem statement:
Redwood needs a reproducible, low-friction playbook that takes a candidate model from a verified bench run to a published Redwood-verified performance profile. Current onboarding is ad-hoc across teams: engineering runs benches, PM curates results, and publishing is manual. This ticket captures a staged validation + publish workflow that can be automated and audited, includes version pinning guidance, canary rollout rules, rollback criteria, and ongoing revalidation cadence.

Goals:
- Define a deterministic staging validation pipeline that mirrors production workload slices (latency P50/P95/P99, throughput, cost/unit).
- Standardize artifacts required for publishing (bench results, sample workload traces, cost model inputs, bias/quality check links).
- Provide a pinning policy for model variants and a default canary rollout with automated metrics gates.
- Create a publish checklist + automated checks to reduce human error and make publishing auditable.
- Specify periodic revalidation cadence and drift triggers to mark profiles stale.

Success metrics:
- Reduce manual review time per profile by 60% (measured as hours spent by PM and Eng per publish).
- 95% of published profiles have full validation artifacts and pass automated gates at publish time.
- Mean time to rollback for a bad profile <= 30 minutes with automated fallback.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented staging-to-publish playbook in Confluence (link in attachments).
- CI pipeline job (profile-staging-validation) that runs benches and outputs a canonical manifest with latency/throughput/cost and artifact links.
- Canary deployment policy template: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated gate at each step based on SLO/delta thresholds.
- Release checklist implemented as checklist file in repo and a lightweight UI action in the Console to trigger publish.
- Periodic revalidation job scheduled (every 30 days) and drift hooks wired to the evals pipeline.

Proposed staging validation flow (high-level):
1) Intake: model PR + model metadata (architecture, weights hash, quantization knobs) and target dataset slices.
2) Bench run: standardized bench harness executes representative workloads (chat, completion, embeddings) at multiple sequence length distributions and concurrency profiles. Outputs: token-level latency histogram, P50/P95/P99, throughput@seqLen, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate.
3) KV/prefix caching sanity: run prefix cache microbench to verify KV cache scaling characteristics.
4) Quality smoke tests: run PM prompt set to validate basic output quality (contains sample prompts and reference metrics).
5) Artifact bundle: bench JSON, perf plots, run logs, PR link, and verified-model-manifest attached to staging job.
6) Automated gates evaluate deltas versus baseline profile(s) and check absolute thresholds. If gates pass, job creates a DraftProfile in the profile registry and notifies reviewers.
7) Manual review window (24-48 hours) for PM/Eng/Research to comment; minor issues can be remediated and bench re-run.
8) Canary publish: template rollout policy applies; profile pinned to a stable model variant ID that maps to both hosted and dedicated runtimes.

Automated gate rules (examples):
- Latency P95 must not regress >15% relative to pinned baseline for given sequence lengths.
- Throughput per GPU must be within -20% of baseline or a documented capacity tag with justification.
- Cost per 1M tokens must not exceed baseline by >25% unless explicit business justification present.
- No single microbenchmark should exceed historical max P99 by >200ms for interactive models.
- KV cache hit rate must be >70% for workloads that exercise prefix caching.

Pinning policy summary:
- All published Redwood-verified profiles must include a pinned model identifier that includes model name, semantic version, checksum (weights hash), and recommended runtime flags (quantization, kernel hints). Example: 'gpt-small-v2+q4_0+sha256:abcd1234'.
- Minor weight-only changes (same checksum) are allowed as patch updates; any checksum change requires staged revalidation and a new profile version.
- Profiles should support a backward-compatible aliasing system (stable alias vs exact pin) to allow safe rollback to an older pinned fingerprint.

Canary rollout template (automated):
- Stage 0: DraftProfile created, no traffic. Notify reviewers.
- Stage 1: Canary-1: 5% traffic for 2 hours. Gate: no P95 regression >10% and error rate unchanged.
- Stage 2: Canary-2: 25% traffic for 4 hours. Gate: P95 regression <=12% and SLI error budget consumption within expected range.
- Stage 3: Ramp to 100% after automated approval or manual signoff.
- Fallback: immediate rollback to previous pinned fingerprint if any gate fails; trigger incident alert to oncall and update profile status to "rolled_back".

Revalidation and staleness rules:
- Schedule a full revalidation every 30 days for production profiles and every 7 days for Canary profiles in active testing.
- Trigger revalidation on upstream infra changes (runtime-1.*), major kernel updates, or if the model's token distribution shifts by >20% (tracked by console histogram diffs).
- Profiles failing revalidation are marked STALE and moved to a suggested-refresh queue; customers with active usage receive an opt-in email and a 14-day grace period before autoswitching to fallback variants.

Observability / dashboard needs:
- Per-profile dashboard tile (latency histograms, throughput, cost trajectory, last validation timestamp, pinned fingerprint).
- Diff view between candidate profile and baseline with highlighted regressions and cost delta.
- Automated audit log entry for every publish/rollback with links to artifacts and reviewer approvals.

Operational checklist for publishing (short):
- [ ] Bench artifacts uploaded and manifest created.
- [ ] Automated gates green.
- [ ] PM review complete (comments resolved).
- [ ] Security & privacy checklist (data handling) verified if model used customer data.
- [ ] Canary policy applied and scheduled.
- [ ] Release note drafted and changelog entry created.

Integration and automation tasks (engineering):
- New CI job profile-staging-validation that produces canonical artifact bundle and manifest (ENG-27108).
- Console API endpoint to create DraftProfile and kick off canary (ENG-27345).
- Profile registry change to store fingerprint + alias mapping + publish metadata (ENG-26890).
- Hook evals pipeline for revalidation triggers (ENG-27910).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Tight automated thresholds may block useful model variants that are costlier but still acceptable; include a documented override flow with explicit business justification.
- Additional staging runs increase onboarding latency and infra cost; mitigate by sampling adaptive bench sizes for low-impact models.
- Pinning to exact fingerprints increases operational safety but can delay quick fixes; use aliasing and fast rollback for agility.

- Week 2 (2025-02-19 -> 2025-02-25): Implement CI job and profile manifest; initial console endpoint stub.
- Week 3 (2025-02-26 -> 2025-03-04): Integrate canary template and audit logging; run two internal onboarding trials.
- Week 4 (2025-03-05 -> 2025-03-15): Iterate on reviewer feedback, finalize Confluence playbook, and flip publish to GA for open-model catalog.
